text:
maya: quick follow-up from the rollout RFC — before we wire automated rollback we need a clear metric contract for canaries. my proposal: 3 signal classes (latency, user-facing errors, quality/regression) + explicit windowing and aggregation keys (model, route, customer tier). also we need to decide retry/idempotency semantics when traffic splits.
chris: +1. please avoid p95-only decisions — use percentile histograms (p50/p90/p99) + traffic-weighted error-rate. thresholds should be relative to baseline (e.g., +40% error-rate over baseline) not absolute.
linh: big callout: client-side retries inflate error-rate. we should require instrumentation of original request-id and client retry count before any metric is considered for rollback. otherwise we get false positives.
samir: can we centralize the decision logic in a small "rollout-decision" service that subscribes to metrics streams and emits commands (promote/rollback/scale)? keeping state in the control plane per-customer will blow up. decision service can also sandbox policies per-tenant.
alex: sketch of a minimal rollout policy that the decision service could consume: ```json
{
  "name": "canary-2pct-3min",
  "target": "model-v3",
  "baseline": "model-v2",
  "split": 0.02,
  "signals": [
    {"type":"error_rate","bucket":"route","window_s":180,"threshold_rel":0.4},
    {"type":"latency_p90","bucket":"model","window_s":180,"threshold_abs_ms":300}
  ],
  "fallback": {"type":"route_swap","target":"model-v2"},
  "safety_checks": {"min_samples":500}
}
```
eva: quick q — how do we treat synthetic probe traffic vs live? IMO probes should be tagged and evaluated separately to avoid skew. synthetic can help fast detection for correctness regressions but not for real-world error spikes.
maya: agreed — intent is 2 channels: synthetic for functional regressions (lower weight) and live for infra/latency regressions (primary). decision service must keep them separate in its rules.
chris: tradeoff: short windows detect faster but increase noise/false rollbacks. we should have a two-stage trigger: a fast alert (3m) that marks the canary as "suspect" and a confirm window (15m) before automated rollback. that gives room for transient blips.
linh: add circuit-breaker semantics: if a metric crosses a severe threshold (eg >200% error-rate) trigger immediate fallback without confirmation. also keep a cool-down to avoid flapping.
samir: interface boundary question: what does the serving runtime need vs control plane? runtime must expose: (1) stable request id + retry metadata, (2) per-request model variant tag, (3) short-lived health signals (queue length, p99 latency). decision service consumes these; runtime enacts routing rules from the control plane. keep contracts minimal.
alex: ops concern: KV cache cold-start on canaries biases latency/quality. we should prime caches for canaries (synthetic warmup) or weight rollout steps to include cache-warmed requests. otherwise canary looks worse than it is.
eva: regarding per-customer rollbacks: we need to support scoped rollbacks (tenant-level) and global ones. scoped policies are more complex (state explosion) but necessary for enterprise customers. suggest default global, opt-in per-tenant policies.
maya: long-term refactor idea: model the rollout logic as a small policy graph (nodes = checks, edges = outcomes) executed by the decision service. policies can be composed and stored in a repo (gitops) so PMs/SEs can author rules without runtime deploys.
chris: telemetry hooks: decision events (suspect, confirm, rollback, promote) must be emitted with reason codes and linked to the metric windows for postmortem. also include a snapshot of sample requests for quality regression debugging.
linh: security note: restrict who can author automatic rollback policies. dangerous if product teams can flip thresholds without guardrails.
samir: action items: 1) define exact metric names and labels (maya + chris, due EOW), 2) proto for decision-service API (samir + alex, 1 week), 3) runtime request-id + retry header contract (linh, 3 days), 4) cache-priming plan for canaries (alex, 2 weeks).
maya: I'll file a follow-up RFC with the metric contract table and a couple of example policies. pulling in sec/release for signoff. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy note: small canary rollout to 2% started for model-v3 at 1795002000 — monitoring channels subscribed. :rocket:
